title: camera_zoom_step comment carries a duplicated tail from the move hunk
evidence: // camera_zoom_step — z scaled by one wheel notch of `delta` (positive = in). of `delta` (positive = in).
detail: The N1 move hunk duplicated the sentence tail: '(positive = in). of `delta` (positive = in).' reads as broken prose — exactly the r3 N14 comment disease class.
recommended_fix: Delete the duplicated tail: '// camera_zoom_step — z scaled by one wheel notch of `delta` (positive = in).'

title: B1 mirror-1 comment cites the wrong fixture's clamp band ([195,585] vs real [234,702]) and wrong drag direction
detail: This fixture is 64x36 tiles x 26px = 1664x936, win 1280x720, fit 0.76923: at zoom 2.0 half_h = 360/1.5385 = 234, real band [234,702] — the [195,585] numbers belong to camera_test's 1040x780 world. Also dy=-200 targets cy 585+130=715, not '< 585'. Assertions are correct; comments mislead.
recommended_fix: Recompute the comment from this fixture: band [234,702], 585 interior, drag targets cy=715; keep the assertion as is.

title: B1 mirror-2 comment claims anchor band [278,762], contradicting its own assertion [416,1248]
evidence:
app2.cam_wx_to = 700 // the wheel's off-center anchor (valid at 2.0: [278, 762])
...
	testing.expect(t, app2.cam_wx_to >= 416 && app2.cam_wx_to <= 1248, "the target sits inside the 2.0 clamp band of the 1664px world")
detail: Real x-band at zoom 2.0 for this fixture: half_w = 640/(0.76923*2) = 416, world_w/2 = 832, band [416,1248]. The comment's [278,762] is not derivable from this fixture and contradicts the assertion two lines below; anchor 700 is valid either way.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment to '[416, 1248]' so comment and assertion agree on the real band.

title: ci-local.sh header + usage still say '10 gates'; the GATES array has 11 entries
evidence:
#   tools/ci-local.sh                 # all 10 gates in a linux container (the ubuntu leg)
...GATES=(
  "Purity + grep gates (ODN-1)|tools/lint.sh"
  [8 more entries]
  "PP_DEBUG overlay builds (compile + the debug test leg)|..."
  "Stats stream replay-identity (live == replay)|..."
  "Input parity (...)|..."
)
detail: Counted GATES entries: 11 (purity, units, builds, golden, palcheck, drift, preview, motion-pixel, PP_DEBUG, stats, parity). Four doc lines (4, 6, 28, 30) still claim 10 — stale after the gate list grew.
recommended_fix: Update header and usage text to 'all 11 gates' / 'the same 11 gates', or derive the count from ${#GATES[@]} in the usage text.

title: B2 gate at the effect leaves dead intent-routing in release (D -> Toggle_Overlay -> no-op) and a stale types.odin comment
evidence:
mouse.odin: case .D:
			append(out, Intent(Toggle_Overlay{}))
exec.odin: case Toggle_Overlay:
		if inp.on_overlay != nil { inp.on_overlay(inp.user, inp) }
types.odin: // Toggle_Overlay — D (PP_DEBUG builds only): the v2-noc debug surface (the
detail: The chosen innermost gate is safe (only true-writer is gated; matches the noc_level behavior-gated precedent) but release compiles the full chain to a no-op. types.odin's 'PP_DEBUG builds only' now describes only the effect, not the mapping — misleading for the next reader.
recommended_fix: Either gate the D mapping (noc_key_test now runs under gate 9's PP_DEBUG test leg anyway) or amend the types.odin comment: 'mapping ungated; the effect is a PP_DEBUG no-op in release'.

title: effect_zoom marks a fully-covered 3-member enum switch #partial, forfeiting exhaustiveness checking
detail: Wheel_Target has exactly three members (Noc_Scroll, Blocked, Zoom — noc_overlay.odin) and all three are cased. A complete switch would fail compilation if a fourth target is added, instead of silently falling through to camera_zoom_at.
recommended_fix: Drop #partial: 'switch rnd.camera_wheel_policy(...)' — the case set is already exhaustive.

title: pullback_feed's fixed ids[8] buffer silently skips the pullback when a frame spawns >8 terminals
detail: A catch-up window frame with 9+ NODE_SPAWNED events caps the walk at 8, found != n_spawns, and the feed returns — the pullback silently drops. The defensive comment justifies dead terminals, not the capacity clamp.
recommended_fix: Size the buffer to the real per-frame spawn ceiling with a pinned comment, or loop camera_newest_terminals over 8-chunks.
